items.name: African elephant
items.clue: Pulls up grass and reaches for leaves, bark and fruit.
items.explanation: African elephants are herbivores. Grass, leaves, bark, roots and fruit all come from plants.

items.name: Giraffe
items.clue: Uses a long tongue to reach leaves high in trees.
items.explanation: Giraffes are herbivores. They browse leaves and other plant parts, often high above the ground.

items.name: Lion
items.clue: Hunts animals such as antelope and zebra.
items.explanation: Lions are carnivores. Their usual wild diet comes from animals, including antelope and zebra.

items.name: Tiger
items.clue: Hunts deer, wild pigs and other animals.
items.explanation: Tigers are carnivores. Deer and wild pigs are examples of the animals they hunt for food.

items.name: Raccoon
items.clue: Finds fruit and nuts, along with insects, crayfish and eggs.
items.explanation: Raccoons are omnivores. Fruit and nuts are plant foods; insects, crayfish and eggs come from animals.

items.name: Brown bear
items.clue: Eats berries and roots, as well as insects, fish and other animals.
items.explanation: Brown bears are omnivores. They eat plant foods and animal foods; what they find changes with the season and location.

items.name: European rabbit
items.clue: Nibbles grass, leaves, buds and roots.
items.explanation: European rabbits are herbivores. Grass, leaves, buds and roots are all plant foods.

items.name: Plains zebra
items.clue: Spends much of its feeding time grazing on grass.
items.explanation: Plains zebras are herbivores. They mostly graze on grass and may also eat leaves and stems.

items.name: Grey wolf
items.clue: Hunts animals such as deer, elk and smaller mammals.
items.explanation: Grey wolves are carnivores. Their usual diet includes large grazing animals and smaller mammals.

items.name: Nile crocodile
items.clue: Catches fish and other animals near the water.
items.explanation: Nile crocodiles are carnivores. Fish, birds and mammals are animal foods.

items.name: Red fox
items.clue: Catches mice and insects, and also eats fruit.
items.explanation: Red foxes are omnivores. Mice and insects are animals, while fruit comes from plants. Hunting does not make their whole diet carnivorous.

items.name: Wild boar
items.clue: Roots around for nuts, roots, insects, worms and eggs.
items.explanation: Wild boars are omnivores. Roots and nuts are plant foods; insects, worms and eggs are animal foods.

rounds.reflection: Choose one omnivore. Name a plant food and an animal food it eats.
